questions.stem: Scenario: Dunmow Group sets an organisation spend limit of 20,000, group limits of 6,000, 8,000 and 6,000, and gives one member a ceiling of 9,000 in the 6,000 group. Which two statements does the page support? (Select two.)

options.text: The groups together exceed the organisation, which breaks the sum
options.says: Ruled out because "a total of exactly 20000 passes and 20001 does not".

options.text: That individual figure is unreachable
options.says: A member's limit is no higher than the smallest group's, since "a member limit above a group's own makes the member limit a number that can never be reached", and the group limits add up exactly to the organisation's total (module 92, page 2).

options.text: The organisation limit is a safety net that makes the other figures optional
options.says: Ruled out because "make the groups add up exactly", because the organisation limit decides first otherwise.

options.text: The three shares sum to the grand total exactly
options.says: A member's limit is no higher than the smallest group's, since "a member limit above a group's own makes the member limit a number that can never be reached", and the group limits add up exactly to the organisation's total (module 92, page 2).

options.text: Nothing is wrong, and a member may exceed a group's limit with consent
options.says: Ruled out because "a member's limit is no higher than the smallest group's", so a figure above the group's cannot stand.

origin.section: Spend limits that add up

questions.stem: Scenario: Rowan Labs has no device management and sets its policy in the admin console, and its security lead wants a stricter policy for the contractors' group alone. What does the page say?

options.text: Ask any administrator to edit the setting for the contractors' group
options.says: Ruled out because it "is edited by an Owner or Primary Owner, not by any administrator".

options.text: Set it in the shared project file that every contractor checks out
options.says: Ruled out because "a policy belongs in managed settings, and the shared file holds what the team agrees for itself".

options.text: It cannot target a subset yet, so a separate profile goes to them
options.says: Server-managed settings apply to everyone in the organisation, and a different policy for one group means a different file or profile deployed to that group (module 92, page 1). They are fetched at startup and refreshed hourly. The page puts it as "per-group policy is not yet supported there".

options.text: Set the stricter values in the console for the group of contractors
options.says: Ruled out because server-managed settings are applied to everyone: "It applies to everyone in the organisation".

origin.section: Server-managed settings and their limits

questions.stem: Scenario: Kinsale Software wants developers to install plugins only from its own marketplace repository, and an engineer sets the managed allowlist of marketplace sources to an empty list to be safe. What happens?

options.text: Every origin is blocked, the firm's and the official one alike
options.says: An empty list blocks every source, the official marketplace included, so allow nothing and allow ours are different lists (module 92, page 2). The company's own repository must be listed to be allowed. The page puts it as "An empty list blocks every source, the official one included".

options.text: Every source is allowed, the firm's own and any public one
options.says: Ruled out because the allowlist is "an allowlist of the sources plugins may come from", and an empty one lists none.

options.text: Only the official source is allowed, and the firm's own is refused
options.says: Ruled out because "Allow all plugins from the official marketplace and block the rest" is rejected, because an empty list blocks the official one too.

options.text: Only the company's source is allowed, and the official one is refused
options.says: Ruled out because "The practice's policy lists one: the company's own marketplace repository", and an empty list names none, so the firm's source is refused too.

origin.section: Where plugins and servers may come from

questions.stem: Scenario: A platform team at Larkin Pay enables Claude Code for an organisation with zero data retention and promises leadership a dashboard of merged pull requests with assistance. What should it check first?

options.text: The baseline of four weeks, since the metrics begin once the baseline period ends
options.says: Ruled out because the baseline is collected before the launch: "the plan takes four weeks of data before the rollout".

options.text: Whether those contribution metrics are available, since they need the GitHub app
options.says: Contribution metrics need the GitHub app and are not available for organisations with zero data retention enabled, so the team checks that before promising them (module 92, page 2). The page puts it as "are not available for organisations with zero data retention enabled".

options.text: The count of lines accepted, since that is the outcome that matters
options.says: Ruled out because "Lines and suggestions accepted are reported and not targeted."

options.text: The seat allowance, since it limits how many merges are recorded
options.says: Ruled out because "a member's use draws from a seat allowance", which concerns spend and not metrics.
